findings.title: Vision setup fails with restored libraries
findings.description: `_initialize_runtime_vision()` no longer supplies the `explored` array to `configure_vision_research()`, while the baseline native implementation still requires an array matching the map's cell count. On this diagnostic branch the platform libraries remain at that baseline, so vision initialization returns `vision_research_input_shape_invalid` for both new and restored worlds.

findings.title: AI countries can no longer start colonies
findings.description: `apply_start_family_expedition` now reads the country handle from `cmd.i64_1` and rejects any command with `expedition_route_hash == 0`. The AI colonization producer in `economy_runtime_country_ai.cpp`, which this PR did not change, still puts the quote token into `i64_1` and never sets `expedition_route_hash`, so every AI start is rejected as `colonization_requote_required`. The same mismatch breaks the AI's duplicate-target check (`pending_family_expedition_target_taken` compares `i64_1` to the country handle) and gives the rejection receipt a bogus country.

evidence.explanation: The AI producer builds START_FAMILY_EXPEDITION commands with `command.i64_1 = tokens[best_i]` and leaves `expedition_route_hash` unset. Those commands are pushed to `_pending_commands` and dispatched through `apply_family_expedition_player_command` into the rewritten `apply_start_family_expedition`. That function now treats `i64_1` as the country and returns `colonization_requote_required` when `expedition_route_hash == 0`. The new `pending_family_expedition_target_taken` also compares `i64_1` against `country_handle`, so queued AI commands never match.

findings.title: Old saves lose explored fog on load
findings.description: `restore_vision_seed` treats a missing VISION section as success without changing its zero-filled `explored` buffer, while the PKFG restorer no longer applies legacy `explored`; the BIO restore similarly accepts a missing section after the geography restorer drops legacy occupancy bits. Pre-change saves have neither native section, and unchanged save versions allow them to load without an error, so the map is fully fogged, species occupancy is regenerated, and a subsequent save persists the lost exploration.

citations.citation: Keynes: new continuation state is versioned, validated and installed atomically

evidence.explanation: The PKFG restore path no longer assigns the saved `explored` array, while native vision initialization zero-fills its buffer and `restore_vision_seed()` leaves that buffer untouched when VISION is absent; the resulting native frame is then copied to the map. The geography restorer drops `cell_bio_occupancy_bits`, and native bio restore likewise reports success without a BIO section. PKFG remains at version 4 and PKSR at v5, so the missing sections in pre-change saves do not cause rejection or migration.

findings.title: Old saves with queued country commands fail to load
findings.description: `RuntimeCountryPodAdapter::decode_command` now accepts only payloads of exactly `COUNTRY_COMMAND_WIRE_SIZE` (400 bytes). Before this PR, country packets stored a raw `memcpy` of `sizeof(RuntimeCountryCommand)`, padding included, so pending country commands in an older PKSR bundle have a different size and fail startup restore with `invalid_country_command_payload_size`.

evidence.explanation: The new decoder requires the exact field-by-field wire size. The removed encoders in `world_ext_country_commands.cpp` and `country_runtime_commands.cpp` copied the whole struct with `memcpy`. On restore, the payload bytes are kept as saved and then decoded by `decode_command`, so the size check rejects them.

findings.title: Oversized scouting orders vanish silently
findings.description: `validate_command()` no longer rejects exploration cell lists exceeding `MILITARY_MAX_EXPLORATION_CELLS`, but `create_exploration_task()` still returns false for them and `apply_command()` ignores that return value. A submitted oversized order can therefore pass admission yet create no task and produce no player rejection.

evidence.explanation: The task creator checks the fixed maximum before copying cells, so this is a silent failure rather than a memory overwrite. The application branch drops its false return and the military publication path exposes only recorded player rejections.

findings.title: Failed peers can stall days forever
findings.description: `worker_main()` removes the timeout paths that faulted prolonged peer waits and failed event-day waits, replacing the remaining peer check with a warning. If a required peer does not complete its day, the worker keeps retrying that day without publishing a commit or transitioning to a fault state.

evidence.explanation: Missing domain input enters a retry wait rather than committing. The replacement `log_slow_peer()` only logs, whereas the deleted timeout and failed-event paths transitioned to a fault.

findings.title: Older saves change future climate
findings.description: `WorldClock.restore_state()` no longer reads the saved anomaly or random-generator state, although `opening_climate_seed()` supplies those clock values when constructing the native climate calendar. For an existing save without the newly introduced native calendar section, loading the world uses the clock's current values instead of its saved climate progression, changing later annual results.

func restore_state(state: Dictionary) -> Dictionary:
	if String(state.get("schema", "")) != "WorldClock" or int(state.get("version", -1)) != 1:
		return {"ok": false, "code": "clock_schema_incompatible", "message": "时钟存档版本不兼容。"}
	current_day = float(state.get("current_day", 0.0))
	_day_carry = clampf(float(state.get("day_carry", 0.0)), 0.0, 0.999999)
	paused = bool(state.get("paused", true))
	speed_multiplier = maxf(float(state.get("speed_multiplier", 1.0)), 0.0)
	visual_day_phase = fposmod(float(state.get("visual_day_phase", 0.25)), 1.0)
	visual_day_phase_held = false
	_last_day = int(state.get("last_day", int(floor(current_day))))
	_last_season = int(state.get("last_season", season_index_for_day(_last_day)))
	_last_year = int(state.get("last_year", year_index_for_day(_last_day)))
	_apply_phase_step_for_speed(speed_multiplier)
	# Applying the speed tier resets the publication cursors. Restore them after
	# the tier thresholds so the next emitted phases match the saved timeline.
	_last_emit_day_phase = float(state.get("last_emit_day_phase", day_phase()))
	_last_emit_season_phase = float(state.get("last_emit_season_phase", season_phase()))
	day_phase_changed.emit(day_phase())
	season_phase_changed.emit(season_phase())

evidence.explanation: The clock save provider delegates restoration to `restore_state()`, while environment initialization takes its starting anomaly and RNG state from `opening_climate_seed()`. Native calendar restoration only overrides that seed if the new section is present.
